# Plan: SPE round r01 for the triage agent

The repo has no `spe/` folder, so this is round r01. Today is 2026-10-21. Round r01 has no earlier round, so the Predict section has no "same as last round" column and the control gate uses a fixed baseline instead.

Defaults I chose: I will build the agent in Python with the Anthropic SDK as one Messages API call that returns structured JSON. The model IDs get pinned after I check current IDs and prices in the claude-api docs.

## 1. Specify

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns exactly one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage. | User: "triage tickets" | Code check: the value is in the enum. |
| R2 | The category matches the support lead's reference label. | User: "correctly" | Code check: exact match against `spe/evals/answers/labels.csv`. |
| R3 | The agent assigns exactly one priority from P1 to P4. | User: "triage tickets" | Code check: the value is in the enum. |
| R4 | The priority matches the reference label. Within one level counts as a near miss. | User: "correctly" | Code check: exact match, plus a separate within-one score. |
| R5 | The agent never under-prioritizes a P1 ticket. | Decision D2 | Code check: recall on reference P1 tickets. |
| R6 | The agent drafts a first reply that addresses the customer's actual issue and invents no facts. | User: "drafts a first reply" | Code check for length and banned promises first. LLM judge with a rubric for relevance and invented facts. |
| R7 | Every response matches the output schema. | Decision | Code check: JSON schema validation. |
| R8 | The average cost per ticket stays at or below $0.02. | User: "cheaply", default D3 | Code check: token counts from the API usage field times the pinned price. |
| R9 | The agent prompt is written without reading the 40 eval tickets or their labels. | Decision (author does not touch the judge) | Transcript scan and a written note in the commit. |

### Open decisions (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Logged default |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What each priority level means. | User, with the support lead | P1 is an outage or data loss for many customers. P2 is a broken core feature for one customer, or billing blocking use. P3 is a non-blocking bug or account change. P4 is a how-to or feature question. |
| D2 | Is a missed P1 a hard fail? | User | Yes. P1 recall below 1.0 blocks a "ship" verdict regardless of other scores. |
| D3 | What "cheaply" means in dollars. | User | $0.02 per ticket on average. |
| D4 | What "correctly" means as a pass bar. | User | Category accuracy at or above 0.85, priority within-one at or above 0.90, reply pass rate at or above 0.80. |
| D5 | Should the reply have a style guide? | User, with the support lead | No style guide in r01. The judge checks relevance, tone, and invented facts only. |

No earlier proposals exist, so no proposals are adopted or rejected in r01.

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each config changes one thing from C1.

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from C1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 (reference) | Sonnet class, pinned | Base prompt with category names and priority definitions from D1 | None |
| C2 | Haiku class, pinned | Same base prompt | Model only |
| C3 | Sonnet class, pinned | Base prompt plus a rubric with 2 synthetic examples per category | Prompt only |
| Naive | No model | Always the most common category and P3 | Baseline for comparison |

The synthetic examples in C3 are written from the category definitions. They are not taken from the 40 tickets.

### Prediction table

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

| Metric | Grader check | C1 | C2 | C3 | Naive | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | `grade_category` exact match | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | 0.30 ± 0.10 | Five categories are mostly distinct, but bug and outage overlap, and so do account and billing. |
| Priority exact accuracy | `grade_priority` exact match | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | 0.68 ± 0.10 | 0.35 ± 0.10 | Priority depends on the support lead's own calibration, which the agent only sees through D1. |
| Priority within one | `grade_priority` within-one | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | 0.80 ± 0.10 | Most misses will be one level off. |
| P1 recall | `grade_p1_recall` | 0.80 ± 0.20 | 0.70 ± 0.20 | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.00 ± 0.00 | The set likely has only 4 to 6 P1 tickets, so one miss moves the score by about 0.2. |
| Schema valid rate | `grade_schema` | 1.00, band 0.98 to 1.00 | 1.00, band 0.97 to 1.00 | 1.00, band 0.98 to 1.00 | not scored | Structured output with a strict schema rarely fails. |
| Reply pass rate | Code checks, then `judge_reply` | 0.85 ± 0.10 | 0.78 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.10 | not scored | Drafting a first reply is easy, but without product docs the agent may invent steps. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | `grade_cost` from usage tokens | 0.014 ± 0.006 | 0.005 ± 0.003 | 0.017 ± 0.006 | 0.000 | About 2,500 input tokens and 400 output tokens per ticket. C3 adds about 1,000 prompt tokens. These are estimates until I check current prices. |

I predict C3 meets the D4 bar and D3 cost cap. I predict C2 is cheapest but misses the D4 category bar. I predict no config reaches P1 recall of 1.0, so D2 will block a ship verdict in r01.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build steps before the eval

1. Create `spe/` with `spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` (this prompt, verbatim), `spec/spec.md`, `spec/disagreements.md`, `plans/r01.md`, and `predictions/r01.yaml`.
2. Move the 40 tickets to `spe/evals/tasks/tickets.jsonl` with ticket text only. Move the labels to `spe/evals/answers/labels.csv`. I will move files with a script and will not open the ticket text.
3. Write the agent in `triage/agent.py` with the output schema in `triage/schema.json`. The schema fields are `category`, `priority`, `reply`, and `reasoning`.
4. Write the graders in `spe/evals/graders/`. The code checks are `grade_schema`, `grade_category`, `grade_priority`, `grade_p1_recall`, `grade_cost`, and `check_reply` (length 40 to 250 words, no refund or timeline promises). `judge_reply` is a pinned Opus-class judge with a 3-item rubric. The judge sees the ticket and the reply but not the config name.
5. Write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with one `ROUND = "r01"` constant.

### Gates, in order

| Gate | Pass rule | On fail |
|---|---|---|
| G1 Grader selftest | The oracle (reference labels) scores 1.0. An empty answer and a deliberately wrong answer both score 0. | Halt. Fix the grader and rerun G1. |
| G2 Control | No earlier round exists. I grade the Naive config instead and confirm the score matches a hand count of the label distribution. | Halt. Report a grader bug. |
| G3 Dry run | 3 cells (C1, C2, C3 on ticket 1) finish, pass schema, and log cost. | Halt and report. |

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` |
| `configs` | `["C1", "C2", "C3"]` (Naive is graded in code, not run) |
| `tasks` | `spe/evals/tasks/tickets.jsonl` (40 tickets) |
| `trials_per_cell` | 3 |
| `split_extra_trials` | Up to 2 more when the 3 trials on a ticket disagree on category or priority |
| `max_extra_trials_total` | 60 |
| `cost_cap_usd` | 30 |
| `trial_tools` | None. Trials get the ticket text only. |

### Integrity rules

- Trials have no file access and never see graders, labels, or predictions.
- The harness scans every transcript for the paths `spe/evals/answers`, `spe/evals/graders`, and `spe/predictions`. Any trial that touched one is voided and logged.
- The harness skips any trial that would cross the cost cap and logs the skip.
- The run ends with a failure analysis that assigns F-numbers and a completeness critic that checks every cell has a score or a logged skip.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

| Item | Count | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Agent calls | 360 plus up to 60 extras | About $6 |
| Judge calls | Same count | About $8 |
| Dry run and selftest | About 10 calls | Under $1 |
| Total | | About $15, capped at $30 |

### Local commits

I will make one local commit after each step. I will not push.

1. `spe r01: spec, transcript, plan, and prediction`
2. `triage: agent and output schema`
3. `spe r01: graders and selftest`
4. `spe r01: workflow harness`
5. `spe r01: eval results`
6. `spe r01: close-out`, tagged `spe-r01`

### After approval, in this order

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` starting with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records the author as "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round: n/a`.
3. Commit (commit 1).
4. Build, commit, run G1 to G3, then launch the Workflow.
5. When the completion notice arrives, write `spe/prediction-log.md`, `spe/failures.md`, a "Proposed for round r02" table in `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`, and `spe/README.md`. Then make commit 6 and tag it.

I will halt and report if the run hits the cost cap, if a leaked answer key or broken grader turns up, or if D1 to D4 need your answer before results mean anything.
critiques: The Requirements (r01) table breaks "triage tickets correctly and cheaply" into R1 to R9. Each row cites a source quote from the prompt and has a Test column, for example "Code check: exact match against spe/evals/answers/labels.csv" for R2 and token cost times the pinned price for R8.

The prediction table gives numeric values with bands for C1, C2, C3, and Naive on every metric, for example category accuracy "0.85 ± 0.08" for C1 and cost "0.005 ± 0.003" for C2. It uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a Why column with a concrete reason. Examples are "bug and outage overlap" for category accuracy, "only 4 to 6 P1 tickets, so one miss moves the score by about 0.2" for P1 recall, and token estimates for cost.

The "After approval" steps copy the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and write spe/predictions/r01.yaml with a do-not-edit header. Commit 1 then happens before the build, the G1 to G3 gates, and the Workflow launch.

The plan runs the eval as a Workflow (spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js) and gates it in order. G1 is a grader selftest with oracle, empty, and wrong answers. G2 is a control check. G3 is a 3-cell dry run. Each gate halts the run if it fails.

The prediction table has a "Grader check" column that ties each metric to a named grader, such as grade_category, grade_priority within-one, grade_p1_recall, grade_schema, check_reply plus judge_reply, and grade_cost. Build step 4 defines each of these graders.

Close-out step 5 writes spe/prediction-log.md and spe/failures.md. It also adds a "Proposed for round r02" table and writes spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml before commit 6 and the spe-r01 tag. The comparison is implied rather than spelled out, but it holds up because the plan defines a hit as "the measured value falls inside the band."
